canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across most papers, the prevailing usage treats this construct as a latent capability of an LLM or agent to select, invoke, and use external tools or APIs appropriately to complete tasks, often including choosing the right tool and arguments or parameters. Many definitions stay close to this core but narrow it to function calling, API call generation, tool selection, or execution, while others broaden it to coordinating multiple tools, sequencing calls, processing tool outputs, or using tools across dialogue settings and complex real-world tasks. A smaller line instead describes tool utilization as observable tool interaction or tool use itself rather than a latent capability, and a few papers foreground particular aspects such as reliability and hallucination reduction, deciding whether to call a tool at all, comprehension of tool documentation and feedback, or integration of conversational history and user profile.

Space of facets. Papers break the construct into recurring facets: selecting the appropriate tool or API, generating valid calls with suitable parameters or code, planning or sequencing multiple calls, coordinating or orchestrating tools, and deciding when to call a tool versus ask follow-up questions, answer directly, or admit inability. Several names are used for closely overlapping ideas, including tool utilization, tool-use proficiency, tool-use capability, tool-calling capability, function-calling capability, tool learning, and tool-using ability, while other labels mark narrower facets such as tool comprehension, flexible tool selection, API call generation capability, planning with functions, contextualised tool use, and tool manipulation. Some papers also place it alongside other agent abilities rather than equating it with them: reasoning is described as preceding function and parameter selection, and text summarization as organizing conversation history after interaction with the environment.

Space of measurement. Papers operationalize the construct with 9 linked measurement instruments, and they also connect it to 2 behavioral indicators, tool use and text summarization. The most frequently used instruments are ToolBench, API-Bank, BFCL, BFCL-v2, and GAIA, followed by 4 others; these linked measures are mostly benchmarks, datasets, or executable function or tool-calling evaluations rather than human evaluation, LLM-as-a-judge, or probes. What they score is usually explicit tool or function calling, planning, retrieval, correction, and fine-grained invocation accuracy, which mostly matches the dominant capability-based definitions, though some papers define tool utilization as observable interaction and one related benchmark discussion notes that existing evaluations often emphasize calling the correct tool and parameters more than deciding when not to call a tool.

Links. Several papers claim a causal relationship from tool use ability to tool use. One paper claims a causal relationship from instruction following ability to tool use ability, stating that models with better instruction-following capabilities achieve greater improvements with high-quality tool instructions, and one paper reports an inverse correlation between irrelevance detection ability and tool use ability. Papers also report that tool use is related to tool use ability, and that reasoning, text summarization, and BFCL are related to tool use ability.

definitions.text: The ability of a large language model to accurately and effectively interact with external tools throughout a task, maximizing successful outcomes while minimizing errors and hallucinations.
definitions.paper: Reducing Tool Hallucination via Reliability Alignment

definitions.text: The latent ability to select appropriate functions and parameters to invoke based on reasoning input, enabling tool use in agent tasks.
definitions.paper: MoRAgent: Parameter Efficient Agent Tuning with Mixture-of-Roles

definitions.text: The underlying capability of an LLM agent to identify and choose the appropriate enterprise tools or APIs required to perform a given subtask.
definitions.paper: Can LLMs Help You at Work? A Sandbox for Evaluating LLM Agents in Enterprise Environments

definitions.text: The latent ability to select and invoke external tools appropriately during task execution.
definitions.paper: Watch Out for Your Agents! Investigating Backdoor Threats to LLM-Based Agents

definitions.text: The general capability of an AI system to effectively select and utilize external tools, such as web browsers or code interpreters, to accomplish tasks.
definitions.paper: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants

definitions.text: The model's latent ability to effectively select and use external tools to solve complex problems.
definitions.paper: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors

definitions.text: The ability of a large language model to effectively select, invoke, and coordinate external tools to solve complex tasks.
definitions.paper: GTA: A Benchmark for General Tool Agents

definitions.text: The latent capacity of an LLM to choose, call, and use external tools appropriately to satisfy user requests across dialogue settings.
definitions.paper: MTU-Bench: A Multi-granularity Tool-Use Benchmark for Large Language Models

definitions.text: The latent ability to interact with external tools and APIs, including functions such as web browsing, code execution, and file uploads.
definitions.paper: Law of the Weakest Link: Cross Capabilities of Large Language Models

definitions.text: The latent ability to choose and sequence external tools effectively when solving multi-modal tasks.
definitions.paper: Multi-modal Agent Tuning: Building a VLM-Driven Agent for Efficient Tool Usage

definitions.text: The capability of an LLM to understand and utilize external tools or APIs to solve problems that it cannot complete independently.
definitions.paper: Tool-Planner: Task Planning with Clusters across Multiple Tools

definitions.text: The degree to which an LLM understands what a tool does, when to invoke it, and how to use it correctly from documentation and feedback.
definitions.paper: From Exploration to Mastery: Enabling LLMs to Master Tools via Self-Driven Interactions

definitions.text: The latent ability of an LLM to effectively leverage external tools to solve complex real-world tasks.
definitions.paper: From Exploration to Mastery: Enabling LLMs to Master Tools via Self-Driven Interactions

definitions.text: The skill of interacting with and controlling external tools or APIs, typically by generating code or commands.
definitions.paper: Divergent Thoughts toward One Goal: LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration System for Electronic Design Automation

definitions.text: The latent ability of a model to determine whether to call a tool, ask for more information, admit inability to answer, or generate a direct response based on the availability and relevance of tools and input completeness.
definitions.paper: When2Call: When (not) to Call Tools

definitions.text: The model's latent ability to understand user requests, select appropriate external tools, formulate correct API calls, and process their outputs.
definitions.paper: ToolFlow: Boosting LLM Tool-Calling Through Natural and Coherent Dialogue Synthesis

definitions.text: The ability to dynamically and accurately choose the most appropriate tool from a large and complex toolkit based on the specific requirements of a given task or scenario.
definitions.paper: MeNTi: Bridging Medical Calculator and LLM Agent with Nested Tool Calling

definitions.text: The underlying ability of a large language model to generate appropriate function calls based on natural language input and a provided list of available functions.
definitions.paper: CONFETTI: Conversational Function-Calling Evaluation Through Turn-Level Interactions

definitions.text: The underlying capability of agents within a system to interact with external tools (e.g., code interpreter, search engine) to extend their functional scope and access real-world data.
definitions.paper: MetaAgent: Automatically Constructing Multi-Agent Systems Based on Finite State Machines

definitions.text: The model's latent ability to produce syntactically and semantically correct code snippets for invoking APIs based on natural language instructions.
definitions.paper: API Pack: A Massive Multi-Programming Language Dataset for API Call Generation

definitions.text: The cognitive capability to decompose complex tasks into manageable steps and determine the appropriate sequence of function calls required to solve them.
definitions.paper: Facilitating Multi-turn Function Calling for LLMs via Compositional Instruction Tuning

definitions.text: The latent capacity of a model to correctly interpret user queries and generate valid function calls with appropriate arguments, given a set of available tools.
definitions.paper: xLAM: A Family of Large Action Models to Empower AI Agent Systems

definitions.text: The specific ability to use tools effectively by integrating information from the conversational history and user profile.
definitions.paper: TAPS: Tool-Augmented Personalisation via Structured Tagging

relationships.paper: Robust Function-Calling for On-Device Language Model via Function Masking
relationships.evidence: API-Bank (Li et al., 2023) provides a comprehensive dataset featuring 2,138 distinct APIs and 1,888 dialogues with 4,149 API calls. This dataset is designed to evaluate LLMs’ tool-utilization capabilities, including planning, retrieval, and API-calling proficiency. (Section 2)

iclr25: Robust Function-Calling for On-Device Language Model via Function Masking
naacl25: ToolFlow: Boosting LLM Tool-Calling Through Natural and Coherent Dialogue Synthesis

relationships.paper: From Exploration to Mastery: Enabling LLMs to Master Tools via Self-Driven Interactions
relationships.evidence: Tool learning enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to interact with external environments by invoking tools, serving as an effective strategy to mitigate the limitations inherent in their pre-training data. (ABSTRACT)

iclr25: From Exploration to Mastery: Enabling LLMs to Master Tools via Self-Driven Interactions
emnlp25: Learning to Ask: When LLM Agents Meet Unclear Instruction

relationships.paper: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
relationships.evidence: GAIA proposes real-world questions that require a set of fundamental abilities such as reasoning, multi-modality handling, web browsing, and generally tool-use proficiency. (ABSTRACT)

iclr24: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants

relationships.paper: GTA: A Benchmark for General Tool Agents
relationships.evidence: Step-by-step mode is designed to evaluate the model’s fine-grained tool-use capabilities. (Section 4.1)

neurips24: GTA: A Benchmark for General Tool Agents

relationships.paper: ToolACE: Winning the Points of LLM Function Calling
relationships.evidence: Experiments are conducted on two representative benchmarks, including BFCL Yan et al. (2024) and API-Bank Li et al. (2023). The two benchmarks are comprehensive and executable function call evaluations specifically designed to assess the ability of LLMs to invoke functions.

iclr25: ToolACE: Winning the Points of LLM Function Calling

relationships.paper: Robust Function-Calling for On-Device Language Model via Function Masking
relationships.evidence: we identified a concerning inverse relationship between the model's ability to accurately execute function calls and its capacity for irrelevance detection

iclr25: Robust Function-Calling for On-Device Language Model via Function Masking

relationships.paper: EASYTOOL: Enhancing LLM-based Agents with Concise Tool Instruction
relationships.evidence: Llama3.1-70B-Instruct outperforms Llama3.1-8B-Instruct with EASYTOOL, indicating that models with better instruction-following capabilities can achieve greater improvements with high-quality tool instructions. (Section 5.1)

naacl25: EASYTOOL: Enhancing LLM-based Agents with Concise Tool Instruction

relationships.paper: ToolFlow: Boosting LLM Tool-Calling Through Natural and Coherent Dialogue Synthesis
relationships.evidence: We evaluated TOOLFLOW’s tool-calling ability on the BFCL. (Section 5.2.1)

naacl25: ToolFlow: Boosting LLM Tool-Calling Through Natural and Coherent Dialogue Synthesis

relationships.paper: ToolFlow: Boosting LLM Tool-Calling Through Natural and Coherent Dialogue Synthesis
relationships.evidence: ToolAlpaca (Tang et al., 2023) establishes a multi-agent simulator. It utilizes GPT-4 (OpenAI et al., 2024) to simulate the return values of tools. The model can make modifications and re-call the tool based on the return values (e.g., error messages). Finally, GPT-4 evaluates the accuracy of Process and Response.

naacl25: ToolFlow: Boosting LLM Tool-Calling Through Natural and Coherent Dialogue Synthesis

relationships.paper: MoRAgent: Parameter Efficient Agent Tuning with Mixture-of-Roles
relationships.evidence: LLMs must first comprehend the user’s query and perform a reasonable analysis and planning, demonstrating the ability of reasoning. Subsequently, it needs to invoke the correct functions with suitable parameters, reflecting the ability of execution.

icml25: MoRAgent: Parameter Efficient Agent Tuning with Mixture-of-Roles

relationships.paper: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
relationships.evidence: “To assess the tool-use capabilities of LLMs, we develop an automatic evaluator, ToolEval” and “We first present ToolBench, an instruction-tuning dataset for tool use”

iclr24: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
